Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, VP of Exploration; Karen Ruiz, VP of Marketing; and Maria Gonzalez, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Harlan.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth across our key basins, with total volumes averaging 285,000 BOE per day, reflecting a 5% increase quarter-over-quarter and 14% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on lifting costs, which fell to $9.85 per BOE, a 12% sequential improvement, thanks to digital tools and water management innovations. We are focused on disciplined capital allocation, balancing dividends, buybacks, and high-return reinvestments. Further, we are working on exploration upside in the Permian and Guyana. We continue to adjust to market volatility with a strong hedge book. We are advancing environmental initiatives that reduced reportable spills by 33% year-over-year. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize our CapEx at $2.4 billion for the full year, delivering peer-leading returns.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Operating income was $950 million, and net income was $680 million. We generated $1.2 billion in free cash flow and returned $550 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt and $3.6 billion in cash.

Let me expand on a few key areas starting with our capital expenditure breakdown for Q3 and year-to-date, covering drilling, completion, and facilities—budget versus actuals. Our full-year 2024 CapEx guidance remains at $2.4 billion, weighted 65% towards the drill bit, with a disciplined focus on our Tier 1 Permian acreage and selective Eagle Ford bolt-ons. We've executed well against this amid WTI averaging $82 per barrel in the quarter and service cost inflation moderating to around 8% year-over-year, down from double-digits in 2023.

Year-to-date as of Q3 end, total CapEx spend came in at $1.85 billion, or 77% of our annual budget—right on plan for our back-half loaded program. Variances were minimal overall, with a $45 million net underspend driven by drilling efficiencies offsetting some completion cost pressures.

Drilling budget was $1.45 billion YTD versus actual $1.38 billion, or 95% of budget. We're under by $70 million, thanks to operational excellence. Drilling represented 59% of total CapEx YTD. In the Permian Delaware Basin—our core engine—we spudded 42 horizontal wells across 12 pads, averaging 12,500-foot laterals. The underspend came from transitioning to in-house optimized bottom-hole assemblies with high-spec PDC bits from Halliburton, boosting ROPs by 22% to over 800 feet per day in the Wolfcamp A and B benches, shaving 3-4 days per well off AFE estimates. Permian AFEs were $850 versus $920 budgeted, though we had a $15 million overrun in Eagle Ford due to torque-and-drag issues in the Austin Chalk with Patterson-UTI SuperSpec rigs, mitigated by Nabors' SmartROS real-time analytics, now at 98% on-bottom efficiency. This builds our D&C inventory to 1,800+ locations at sub-$50 breakevens at $70 WTI. Q4 drilling spend accelerates to $420 million with two additional Walker Ridge pads.

Completion budget $780 million YTD versus actual $810 million, or 104% of budget—a $30 million overrun, 35% of total CapEx. We completed 48 wells, using engineered completions with diverter tech and 45-foot stage spacing in Wolfcamp C. In Permian Midland, our Big Fracs with 3.5 million pounds of sand per well and SLB's GeoSphere mapping drove 15% uplift in 30-day IPs. Overrun from Permian 100-mesh sand up 12% to $55/ton and accelerating two Eagle Ford pads with ProFrac zipper fracs at $18 million premium. Costs per lateral foot held at $950, flat YoY with 10% more proppant. Hybrid slickwater-gel unlocks 20%+ EURs, de-risking 400 locations. Q4 at $280 million, tapering.

Facilities budget $170 million YTD versus $160 million actual, 94%—under by $10 million, 7% of CapEx. Focused on water management and electrification. In Delaware, two 20,000 bbl/day produced water facilities with DNOW modular designs support 100% recycled water by 2025, saving $5 million via EnerCorp prefab. Eagle Ford deferred compressor tie-ins; advancing 50 MW solar microgrid with NextEra at $12 million to cut Scope 1 emissions 15%. Hedged tubulars at $1,200/ton. Yields 3x ROI on reduced LOEs at 85% utilization. Q4 $75 million for LACT upgrades and gas gathering.

These variances enabled recycling $100 million savings into three high-NGV bolt-ons at $12,000/acre in Northern Delaware. CapEx intensity at $7.50/BOE, 80%+ IRR at strips, outperforming peers for 15% growth to 250,000 BOE/d by year-end.

Shifting to lifting costs per BOE, our lease operating expenses averaged $9.85 per BOE in Q3, a 12% sequential drop from $11.20 in Q2 and 22% year-over-year from $12.65, our lowest ever, ahead of sub-$10 target. Over five years, -11% CAGR from $15.40 in 2019. First quartile peers; Permian at $8.20/BOE down 15% YoY, Eagle Ford $7.50, Bakken $11.40 up slightly, GoM $18.50 offset by ramps.

Initiatives include AI predictive maintenance via Schlumberger Delfi on 85% Permian pads, cutting downtime 28% and workovers 35% for $1.20/BOE savings; digital twins extending ESP run lives to 850 days; $150 million DLE with Standard Lithium recycling 70% Permian water, disposal from $0.80 to $0.35/bbl; simul-fracs compressing cycles 20%; multi-year contracts 15-20% below spot; incentive staffing for 10% efficiency, TRIR 0.12. Targeting $8.50/BOE year-end with solar-battery hybrids and Bakken divestitures. Sub-$45 breakevens at $78 WTI, 60%+ FCF returns at $60 oil.

On debt levels, total debt $14.8 billion at quarter-end, down 8% QoQ from $16.1 billion and 15% YoY. Senior notes $10.2 billion at 4.8% average coupon, 5.2-year maturity; refinanced $1.5 billion 2026 notes to 5.25% 2031, saving $150 million interest. Bank debt $3.1 billion on $4.5 billion revolver with $1.4 billion undrawn, 4.1x EBITDA headroom. Other $1.5 billion project finance.

Net debt $11.2 billion, down $1.6 billion QoQ, $2.8 billion YoY, with $3.6 billion cash, $800 million lines, $2.1 billion liquidity. In $11-13 billion target. Leverage: net debt/TTM EBITDA 2.6x from 3.1x, TTM EBITDA $4.3 billion up 12%; gross 3.4x below 4.0x target; debt-to-book 28%. Tighter than peers, $3.8 billion YTD OCF, 85% FCF conversion.

Capital allocation priorities: $1.8 billion Q3 FCF, $7.2 billion full year up 15%. First dividends: 10% hike to $0.65/share quarterly, $2.52 annual, 3.8% yield, 35% payout, 2.5x coverage, 12% CAGR since 2020. Buybacks: $1.9 billion YTD of $4 billion auth, $650 million Q3 at $62/share, 8% EPS boost, EV/EBITDA 4.2x. Reinvestment $6.8 billion capex: upstream $4.4 billion Permian laterals 12,500 ft, $650/ft, $35 breakevens, 1,800 boe/d IP; Guyana $500 million; midstream $1.4 billion pipelines; downstream/new energy $1.0 billion CCUS, LNG. Hedged 60% 2025 at $75. Permian 85% FCF.

Finally, 2025 CapEx guidance $6.2-6.8 billion for 5% growth to 850,000 boe/d. Development $4.0-4.4 billion: Permian $2.8 billion 250 wells $8-9 F&D; GoM $800 million tie-backs. Exploration $1.0-1.2 billion: Guyana $600 million 1.5 Bboe potential, Permian/Eagle Ford $300 million. Maintenance $700-900 million water recycling 90%. Tech/low-carbon $500 million: Delfi AI, CCUS 5 MMtpa $150 million credits, hydrogen. 22% IRR, $35-40 breakevens at $75 WTI, $4.5 billion FCF base.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute effectively. Production averaged 285,000 BOE/d total, 175,000 bbl/d oil up 4% QoQ 17% YoY, gas 660 MMcf/d or 110,000 BOE/d up 6% QoQ 10% YoY. Permian 205,000 BOE/d 72%, 28 Delaware wells 1,800 BOE/d IP 12% above type curve, 12,500 ft laterals. Eagle Ford 43,000 BOE/d up 3% QoQ, GoM 28,000 up 9% Winterfell tie-back. Stage 5 completions 15% EUR uplift to 1.2 MMBOE, AI forecasting. Q4 guide 290-298k BOE/d, oil 178-182k. Divested Bakken gas, Permian bolt-ons. We successfully brought Permian Delaware pads online, contributing to growth. Progress on cost reductions via automation and recycling.

Now I will turn it over to David Patel for an update on exploration activities.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about our program. We completed a successful seismic survey in Permian Delaware Basin and plan 20 exploration wells next year. These have potential to add significant reserves, mirroring Guyana Block 7 appraisals with ExxonMobil analogs, 1.5 billion boe gross mean.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Karen Ruiz to discuss our marketing strategy.

Karen Ruiz: Thank you, David. We are optimizing to maximize production value. Strong demand for Permian crude in Gulf Coast and Asia markets, expanding customer base via Matterhorn Express expansions and LNG offtake commitments. Differentials tightened, significant impact on realizations at $42/BOE.

I will now turn it over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Karen. We are committed to reducing our footprint. Significant progress cutting GHG emissions via electrification and CCUS, investing in renewables like solar microgrids. Improving water management with 90% recycling, protecting biodiversity through drone patrols and bioremediation.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with XYZ Capital. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the CapEx variances this quarter?

Mike Harlan: Good morning, John. John Ramirez can provide the color. But high-level, we came in under budget on drilling due to ROP gains and facilities efficiencies, slight over on completions from sand costs, net savings recycled to bolt-ons.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Greenstone Partners. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. What are your expectations for lifting costs and debt levels into 2025?

John Ramirez: Good morning, Emily. On lifting costs, targeting $8.50/BOE consolidated with further electrification and divestitures. Debt-wise, exiting 2024 below $11 billion net, 2.4x leverage, targeting 2.0x by end-2025 via $6-7 billion cumulative FCF.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Horizon Advisors. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee: Could you please provide more color on production trends QoQ and YoY?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Tom. As detailed, 5% QoQ to 285k BOE/d, 14% YoY, oil 17% YoY to 175k bbl/d, gas 10% YoY despite curtailments. Permian drove with new IPs outperforming type curves.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Vanguard Energy. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Good morning, Rachel. Positive seismic in Delaware and Guyana appraisals de-risk long-cycle portfolio, adding high-IRR reserves to support 5% growth, organic focus ahead of M&A, maintaining Tier 1 inventory.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Davis with Pinnacle Securities. Please go ahead.

Mark Davis: What is the outlook for your marketing strategy and new energy tie-ins in the coming years?

Karen Ruiz: Good morning, Mark. Strong Gulf Coast/Asia demand, midstream JVs lock 70% fee-based, LNG from Mozambique positions for 20% global demand surge, enhancing realizations amid transition.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Greenleaf Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks. Good morning, team. Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets, specifically spills, incidents, and remediation efforts? Any color on trends or initiatives?

John Ramirez: Good morning, Sarah. Maria Gonzalez will provide the details.

Maria Gonzalez: Thanks, John. Sarah, great question. Environmental stewardship is core. In full-year 2023 equivalent metrics for Q3 trends, 12 reportable spills, down 33% from 18 in 2022, three-year -22% CAGR toward sub-10 by 2025. Volume 148 barrels, 41% down, SVI 0.12 bbl/MMBOE below Permian 0.28, U.S. 0.35 EPA.

Upstream 8 spills 92 bbl: Permian 5 Tier 2 <5 bbl wellhead, Eagle Ford 2 water 3 bbl, Bakken 1 SWD 12 bbl. Midstream 3 pipeline 45 bbl gathering. GoM 1 11 bbl mud contained. Zero high-consequence, 47 incidents down 28%, TRIR 0.12.

Remediation: 17 min response, 98% recovery, $14.2 million spend, $96k/bbl cost down 35%. Initiatives: DAS/DTS 85% Permian 4,200 miles detecting 62% pre-release; 150 drones hyperspectral 14 near-misses; SLB bioremediation 95% in 45 days; PIMP EMAT 220 miles recoated. Permian Zero campaign cut 45% YoY. Sustainalytics 12.5/100, $1.2 billion green bonds. 2024 <100 bbl, full DAS, $50 million closed-loop water. Uptime 99.8%, NPS +15%, net-zero 2040 path.

Sarah, does that cover it?

Sarah Jenkins: That's comprehensive—thanks, Maria.

Maria Gonzalez: Our pleasure.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Harlan for closing remarks.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
